identity.real_world_identity_notes: The RFactor2 telemetry label Radical SR3 00 Left Drive maps to the Radical SR3 RSX. The 00 suffix is not a 2000 model year: Studio 397's official release names the car SR3 RSX and says the simulator includes left- and right-hand-drive variants. Independent Radical material places the RSX in the Gen 3 model line introduced for 2015, with the RSX run ending in 2020. The real car is a lightweight prototype-style sports racer with six forward gears, paddle sequential shifting, a clutch-assisted pull-away, automatic ignition cut for flatshift upshifts, and an auto blipper for downshifts.

The exact rFactor2 telemetry class and official Studio 397 release identify the simulated model as the Radical SR3 RSX and explain the left-drive suffix. Radical-origin documentation independently establishes the RSX generation, six-speed paddle-shift controls, pull-away clutch procedure, flatshift/ignition-cut behavior, and auto-blipped downshifts. A repository scan found no existing curated Radical SR3 RSX record, so this case proposes a new record.

claims.basis: The exact rFactor2 telemetry class and official Studio 397 release identify the simulated model as the Radical SR3 RSX and explain the left-drive suffix. Radical-origin documentation independently establishes the RSX generation, six-speed paddle-shift controls, pull-away clutch procedure, flatshift/ignition-cut behavior, and auto-blipped downshifts. A repository scan found no existing curated Radical SR3 RSX record, so this case proposes a new record.

The RSX owner manual gives the gear order through 6th and states that the driver can shift all the way to 6th after pulling away. The manual documents a paddle-shift system with an ordered 1-N-2-3-4-5-6 gear sequence, establishing sequential gearbox behavior. The relevant manual section is explicitly titled PaddleShift Controls and describes paddle requests for the ordered gears. The documented gear order is 1-N-2-3-4-5-6, which is a sequential pattern rather than an H gate. The manual explicitly instructs the driver to depress the clutch to pull away and select first from neutral. The manual says the automatic ignition cut allows the driver to flatshift up the gearbox; no driver clutch operation is prescribed for those running upshifts. Flatshifting is explicitly enabled by the automatic ignition cut, so the manual does not require a throttle lift for the running upshift. The owner manual explicitly states that the SR3 is fitted with automatic ignition cut and connects it to flatshift upshifts. The documented upshift technique is a flatshift assisted by automatic ignition cut; the manual does not call for a manual throttle blip on an upshift. The owner manual assigns the automatic blipper to the downshift procedure and describes the upshift assistance as automatic ignition cut, not an automatic upshift blip. The owner manual explicitly says the driver does not have to blip the throttle on the way down. The owner manual explicitly states that the SR3 is fitted with an auto blipper; its statement that the driver need not blip on downshifts identifies the automatic system as the source of the blip. The RSX row specifies a closed-circle wheel. Under the repository rim definition, a continuous closed circle is round. The RSX row specifies a separate AIM MXL/MXL2 mounted to the dash panel, so the display is not integrated into the wheel rim. The RSX wheel is specified as closed-circle, which establishes that rim material joins over the top under the repository's open-top definition. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.
